hyps.why: Adding a conv where no edge existed creates a new useful path, a larger gain than replacing an existing op.
Turning a missing edge into a 3x3 conv adds a path to the output rather than swapping out an existing contributor.
With fewer alternative paths into the output node, the direct input-output edge carries more of the network's capacity.
If node 1 does not feed the output directly, a conv on its incoming edge has less influence on the final features.
When node 2 has no edge to the output, operations feeding node 2 are effectively dead.
A conv into node 2 is useless when node 2 is disconnected from the output.
Without the direct input-output edge, removing another output edge is more damaging and can disconnect the cell.
Deleting a strong 3x3 conv costs much more accuracy than deleting a weaker op.
Adding a residual path where none existed improves trainability more than replacing an existing op with skip.
Replacing the best parametric op with a parameter-free pool removes much more capacity than replacing a weaker op.
